title: Quasi-affine scheme representability descends over a faithfully flat affine base
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and use algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] and sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $p:V\to U$ be a flat surjective morphism [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism] between affine $S$-schemes, and let $f:X\to U$ be a morphism from an algebraic space. Suppose $X\times_UV$ is represented by a quasi-affine scheme. Then $X$ is represented by a quasi-affine scheme. Here quasi-affine means isomorphic to a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. No representability, separation, finite-type, or finite-presentation hypothesis on $f$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0423 (lemma-descending-property-quasi-affine), affine flat-surjective reduction in its proof, lines 1690-1719; quasi-affine spaces as in spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03WL (definition-quasi-affine).

proof.text: The affine open cover $\{U\}$ has affine inverse image $V$, so [pqf-lem-affine-local-target] makes $p$ affine. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3), it is quasi-compact. For each affine open $B\subseteq U$, the inverse image $p^{-1}(B)$ is quasi-compact and maps onto $B$. Choose a finite affine open cover of this inverse image; its images cover $B$. Flatness restricts to these opens because their local rings are unchanged. These are exactly the conditions of [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering], so $\{p\}$ is fpqc. Choose a quasi-affine scheme $P$ representing $X\times_UV$, with projection $a:P\to V$. Applying [lem-a1-quasi-affine-target-locality] to the one-member affine cover $\{V\}$ shows that $a$ is a quasi-affine morphism.

The two pullbacks of $P$ to $V_2=V\times_UV$ represent the same functor: its $T$-points are triples $(x,v_0,v_1)$ with $f(x)=p(v_0)=p(v_1)$. Define $\phi:\operatorname{pr}_0^*P\to\operatorname{pr}_1^*P$ by retaining $x,v_0,v_1$ and changing the distinguished $P$-coordinate from $(x,v_0)$ to $(x,v_1)$. This natural bijection of representable functors is a scheme isomorphism: evaluate it on the identity of each representing scheme to obtain mutually inverse morphisms. Over $V\times_UV\times_UV$, both $\phi_{12}\phi_{01}$ and $\phi_{02}$ send $(x,v_0)$ to $(x,v_2)$ and retain all three ordered base coordinates. Thus the cocycle of [def-pd-descent-datum] holds. This spells out the omitted verification in Tag 0423, using the fibre-product functors of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

Apply [lem-trf-quasi-affine-fpqc-effective-descent] with its $(A,B,V)$ equal to $(V,U,P)$. Step 1 supplies its singleton fpqc cover and quasi-affine morphism; step 2 supplies its scheme descent datum. Obtain a scheme $b:Y\to U$ and an isomorphism $\alpha:Y\times_UV\xrightarrow{\sim}P$ over $V$ inducing exactly $\phi$. No finite-presentation assumption is required. The base change of $b$ is therefore the quasi-affine morphism $a$. By [lem-sfb-scheme-quasi-affine-fpqc-descent], $b$ is quasi-affine. Since $U$ itself is an affine open of $U$, its inverse image is all of $Y$; the definition [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism] makes $Y$ a quasi-affine scheme.

For any $U$-scheme $T$, set $T_V=T\times_UV$. By [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change], $T_V\to T$ is an fpqc covering. An element $y\in\operatorname{Mor}_U(T,Y)$ restricts to a map $T_V\to Y\times_UV$; applying $\alpha$ and the projection $P\to X$ gives $x_V:T_V\to X$. On $T_V\times_TT_V$ the two maps agree: compatibility of $\alpha$ with the datum says they are related by $\phi$, and step 2 shows that $\phi$ retains the $X$-section. By [lem-a1-algebraic-space-fpqc-sheaf] there is a unique $x:T\to X$ restricting to $x_V$. It is over $U$: its composite with $f$ agrees with the given $T\to U$ on $T_V$, so uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] with target $U$ makes them equal.

Conversely, for $x:T\to X$ over $U$, the pair $(x|_{T_V},T_V\to V)$ gives a map $T_V\to P$, hence via $\alpha^{-1}$ a map $y_V:T_V\to Y$. On $T_V\times_TT_V$, the two $P$-lifts are related by the explicit $\phi$ of step 2. Since $\alpha$ induces this datum, their $Y$-coordinates agree. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] with target $Y$ to obtain a unique $y:T\to Y$. Its composite with $b$ is the prescribed $T\to U$ by the same uniqueness with target $U$. The constructions in this step and step 4 are inverse: after the fpqc covering they are inverse by $\alpha^{-1}\alpha=1$ and $\alpha\alpha^{-1}=1$; equality on $T$ follows from the uniqueness clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] and [lem-a1-algebraic-space-fpqc-sheaf].

The bijections $\operatorname{Mor}_U(T,Y)\simeq\operatorname{Mor}_U(T,X)$ commute with every morphism of $U$-schemes: pullback preserves the local formulas using $\alpha$, and uniqueness of the glued sections preserves their equality. For an arbitrary $S$-scheme $T$, decompose both sets of $S$-maps by their composites $T\to U$ and apply these bijections to each fixed composite. They give inverse natural transformations $h_Y\simeq X$, hence an isomorphism of algebraic spaces over $S$, since their morphisms are natural transformations [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Thus the quasi-affine scheme $Y$ of step 3 represents the original $X$.
